newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy to meet Israel's Netanyahu on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to meet Israel's Netanyahu on Hebron.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will meet U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross ahead of a possible summit with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday to seal a deal on Hebron, an official said.
But Palestinians said the two sides were still far from reaching a deal and that no preparations had been made for an Arafat-Netanyahu meeting.

"Ross is going up to the north where Netanyahu's visiting the navy to meet him. I presume he wouldn't go up there unless he thought there was a good chance of sealing the agreement today," said Netanyahu's top adviser David Bar-Illan.
Asked if Netanyahu would meet Arafat on Sunday, Bar-Illan said: "It may happen."
Arafat's aide Nabil Abu Rdainah said no arrangements had been made for a summit with Netanyahu.
"There are deep differences between the two positions. The same disputed issues are still disputed," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said.

Bar-Illan, Netanyahu's director of communications and policy planning, said Israeli and Palestinian negotiators had agreed on most details for implementing a long-overdue Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron and were awaiting Arafat's consent.
"Obviously they wouldn't meet if they didn't feel the time was ripe for tying up loose ends and reaching the agreement," he told Reuters.
Arafat was due to leave Gaza on Monday on a European tour of several days.
Bar-Illan said there would probably be no signing ceremony for the agreement, contrary to earlier Israel-PLO peace deals.

Israel agreed more than a year ago to withdraw its troops from parts of Hebron but Netanyahu, elected last May, insisted on adjusting the agreement to help safeguard 400 Jewish settlers who live among 100,000 Palestinians in the West Bank town.
